label: copy-phase input b (fed-back b), from the 3rd output on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is b (i.e. b was the previous output), at recall_idx >= 2. Nearly 100% of activation mass is on input b. It never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, even when b is input there, and it is almost silent on b at recall_idx 1. Activation is weaker at recall_idx 2 than later. In a run of consecutive bs the first copied b is strongest and later ones decay (about 1.0, 0.5, 0.25 of max). Some predicted b steps stay inactive (precision 0.86 on dev), mostly early in the copy.

issues: The false positives follow a pattern but are graded, and the explanation already mentions them. On dev, about 7.8k of the roughly 10.3k false positives are at recall_idx 2, where precision is 0.53 across 16.7k predicted steps. Precision is 0.89 at recall_idx 3, 0.96 at 4 and 0.98 at 5 and above.

At recall_idx 2, precision rises steadily with L: 0.12 at L=3, 0.45 at L=4, 0.70 at L=9. Precision is very low (0.117) when the previous input was also b (first_tok == b), which fits the reported decay over runs of b. Because the drop is gradual, no clean split can be written as a predicate.

Refinements tried on the test split barely moved F1: adding t>=7 gave 0.927, L>=4 gave 0.927, recall_idx>=3 gave 0.903, (recall_idx>=3) | (recall_idx==2 & L>=8) gave 0.920, and prev_tok != b gave 0.917. None is a meaningful improvement over 0.924.

Each factual claim checked out. There are 0 activations in the original phase and 0 on <DEL>. recall_idx 1 has only 82 active steps out of 500k. Input b carries 100% of the activation mass. Activation is weaker at recall_idx 2. When the previous input is also b, precision drops to 0.67, which fits decay in runs.
The 142 test-split missed activations hold 0.0% of the activation mass and are scattered noise (mostly small activations on the first copied token).
